message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also known as *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduces Hogwarts and the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; explores the mystery of the Chamber of Secrets. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the rise of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s backstory and Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Seventh and final book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published online during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 | Companion book to the Harry Potter films; also serves as a fictional textbook within the wizarding world. |
| **Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald** | 2018 | A companion book to the second film in the Fantastic Beasts series. |

These titles have garnered massive popularity worldwide, with the Harry Potter series becoming one of the best‑selling book franchises ever. If you’re looking for more details about any particular book or need recommendations based on your interests, feel free to ask!
